metaDescription: Digital marketing for Oklahoma businesses: SEO, paid ads, social media, websites and video for Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Norman, Edmond and rural communities.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Oklahoma businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Oklahoma's economy stands on energy, agriculture, aerospace and the enterprises of its tribal nations, and most of its people live in or around two metros that do not think alike. We plan campaigns for the part of the state you serve and the kind of buyer you sell to.

sections.heading: Oklahoma City, Tulsa and everywhere else
paragraphs: Oklahoma City is the capital and the larger metro, covering a very wide area with suburbs such as Edmond, Moore, Yukon and Midwest City. State government, energy companies, a major Air Force maintenance base and a large medical district anchor it. Norman, just to the south, is home to the University of Oklahoma.

Tulsa, in the northeast, was built by oil money and still shows it in its art deco downtown. Today it mixes energy with aircraft maintenance, manufacturing and a lively arts scene, and suburbs like Broken Arrow, Owasso and Jenks hold much of the family spending. Tulsa and Oklahoma City have separate television markets, separate loyalties and a friendly rivalry, so advertising written for one can sound off in the other.
Beyond the two metros are Stillwater and its university, Lawton beside Fort Sill, Enid with its grain elevators, and ranching and farming country reaching to the Panhandle.

sections.heading: Industries that set the pace
paragraphs: Oil and natural gas remain central. When prices are strong, service companies hire and spending rises across the state; when they fall, budgets tighten quickly. Cattle and wheat shape the rural economy. Aerospace is a quiet giant, from military aircraft maintenance in Oklahoma City to airline maintenance and parts manufacturing in Tulsa.

The tribal nations headquartered in Oklahoma are among its largest employers. They operate casinos and resorts, health systems, manufacturing and other businesses, and they are important customers and partners for local suppliers.
bullets: For energy and aerospace suppliers: capability pages, certifications and search visibility for precise services.
For agricultural businesses: content tied to calving, planting, harvest and sale seasons.
For hospitality and entertainment: campaigns that reach drive-in visitors from Texas, Kansas and Arkansas.
For recruiters in every sector: careers pages and job ads that load fast on a phone.

sections.heading: Storm season and the home services rush
paragraphs: Spring in Oklahoma means severe weather. Hail and tornadoes damage roofs, vehicles, fences and windows, and demand for repair appears overnight. Homeowners are wary of crews that arrive from out of state after a storm, and they look for an Oklahoma address, a long review history and proof of insurance. Local roofers, body shops, restoration firms and storm shelter installers should have pages, ad copy and budgets prepared before the season, so campaigns can be switched on for the affected area the same day. Hot summers then hand the urgency to air-conditioning companies.

sections.heading: How Oklahomans choose a business
paragraphs: This is a relationship-driven state. People value a firm that is locally owned, answers the phone and is known in the community through schools, churches and sports. Online, that means reviews from recognisable local customers, photos of your own staff and trucks, and a clear statement of the towns you serve. Many searches come from small communities well outside the metros, so service areas and location pages need to reach as far as your vehicles do.

presence: TDM works with Oklahoma businesses remotely. There is no TDM office in the state. We meet by video call and share plans, drafts and reports online.

faqs.q: Does TDM have an office in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: No. We work remotely with businesses across Oklahoma, using video calls and shared reporting.

faqs.q: Should I market differently in Tulsa and Oklahoma City?
faqs.a: Yes. Each metro has its own suburbs, competitors, media and local pride. Use separate campaigns, place names and landing pages for each one.

faqs.q: How can a local roofer compete after a hailstorm?
faqs.a: Prepare before the season. Keep your business profile and reviews current, publish storm damage pages for the towns you serve, and have ads ready to switch on by area. Show your Oklahoma address, licence and insurance clearly.

faqs.q: How much is digital marketing for an Oklahoma company?
faqs.a: Cost depends on scope, including the channels, the area covered and the amount of content. We prepare a quote after a free consultation.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements and brief, your current website and your competition. The timeline is agreed in the plan.
